Subject: a young Spartan king representing the two royal houses as a social estate. Broad athletic shoulders, short dark curly hair, a modest gold diadem band and dignified amused smile. Wears a crimson royal cloak over a short ivory Greek chiton, restrained bronze scale chest armor, Greek meander edging and leather sandals. He carries a complete bronze Corinthian helmet with dark red horsehair crest under one arm, the other hand rests confidently at his waist. Two separate SMALL ROUND seal medallions hang side by side at his belt to suggest the two independent crowns, no symbols resembling real-world logos. Regal and martial but charmingly comic, not an emperor, no scepter, no crown towers. Both feet fully visible. No words on anything.

Subject: a Perioek, an hereditary landed lord and head of a Greek city-house, not a common craftsman. One fit muscular young man about 26 with closely cropped auburn hair, a neat short beard, raised eyebrow and proud amused expression. Wears an elegant dark teal Greek chlamys with ivory meander edging over a sleeveless ivory chiton and a small bronze breastplate; noble but clearly Spartan-Greek rather than Roman or Renaissance. His muscular forearms are visible. He balances a SMALL stylized Greek fortified hilltop-acropolis model on one palm (low stone wall and Greek colonnaded hall, NOT a medieval fairytale castle); the other hand holds a short rolled land charter with a wax seal, no writing. Broad leather belt, one plain signet ring, short bronze greaves and leather sandals. The compact acropolis model is fully visible, held naturally, not an entire landscape. Complete head-to-toe figure with ample transparent margins, BOTH feet visible.

Subject: a Doryad, a lower landed warrior noble comparable to a knightly lord, not a king. One fit muscular young adult man age 23, short black hair, clean-shaven with a spirited cheeky grin. Wears an OPEN simple bronze Greek pilos helmet so his young face remains visible, a compact bronze chest cuirass, dark moss-green short chiton, ivory shoulder mantle with narrow Greek meander border, leather belt and sandals with bronze greaves. One hand firmly holds a straight ashwood spear vertically, with its whole spearhead and butt end fully inside the frame; the other arm carries a small plain round hoplon with a simple ivory geometric chevron. One LARGE stylized iron fortress-key hangs visibly at his belt as a sign of a granted stronghold; NO crown, diadem, royal medallions, sword or additional held props. Amusing proud stance, strongly built arms and legs, sturdy short comic proportions. Both sandal soles visible. Generous clear transparent margin beyond spear tip, helmet, cloak and feet.

Subject: an Eleuther, one of Phalantia's rare free citizens from a house that bought its freedom, now a capable independent town merchant. One fit muscular young man age 25, short wavy dark brown hair, clean-shaven and a clever warm confident smile. Greek short mustard-ochre chiton with simple cream border and a compact olive shoulder-cloak, a soft shallow Greek traveling cap, sturdy leather belt and open Greek sandals; no Roman toga, no Renaissance coat. His strong forearms and calves are visible. One hand carefully holds a small BRASS BALANCE SCALE with two empty pans hanging from a simple crossbar, the other hand presents a rolled freedom charter bearing one red seal but NO LETTERING. A modest coin pouch hangs from his belt. Relaxed proud upright posture, slight humorous eyebrow. This is a free civilian, no weapons, no armor, no crown, no chains. Complete figure and both sandals fully in frame with wide transparent margins; scale pans and document fully visible.

Subject: a Helot, an unfree dependent agricultural laborer in Phalantia. One fit muscular young adult man age 24, closely cropped dark-blond hair, clean-shaven, strong arms and calves, with an earnest slightly weary but determined expression and a small wry mouth. Bareheaded, wearing a plain coarse warm-grey sleeveless Greek work chiton tied by a simple cord, hem just above the knees, inexpensive worn leather sandals. BOTH hands support a large simple wicker HARVEST BASKET at waist height containing wheat sheaves and a few turnips; a small BLUNT WOODEN planting dibber is tucked INSIDE the basket, clearly an agricultural tool. No weapons, no armor, no coin pouch, no jewelry, no signet, no crown, no freedom charter, no chains, no wounds or humiliating pose. The clothing and tools are entrusted work items rather than symbols of personal property. Upright working posture, not bent double. Keep the gentle flat storybook comic language while showing plain hard-working dependent status; not celebratory slavery. Complete head-to-toe figure, all basket reeds and BOTH sandal soles visible, wide transparent margins.

Subject: a Xenos, a foreign visitor entering Phalantia with official permission and a local host's guarantee. One fit muscular young adult man age 25 with warm medium-brown skin, short black curls, short neatly trimmed beard and a pleasantly hopeful, self-assured expression. He is a respectable foreign merchant traveler, neither a beggar nor a king. Wears a well-kept indigo travel tunic and compact cream wrapped headcloth with a rust-red band, light grey-blue knee-length traveling mantle, leather sandals and a sturdy leather travel satchel over one shoulder; subtly eastern Mediterranean fantasy clothing, no European Renaissance costume. His muscular forearms and calves remain visible. One hand raises a modest rolled ENTRY PERMIT with TWO small wax seals in different colors but NO LETTERING; the other rests on the satchel strap. A separate small round bronze host-guarantee token hangs from the permit cord, no writing or readable symbols. Friendly upright traveling stance, all props close to the body so the silhouette stays clear. No weapons, armor, crowns, chains, poverty caricature or expensive overflowing treasure. Complete full figure including both sandal soles with wide transparent margins.
